rationale: Two randomized ground-anise studies give favorable gastrointestinal pain comparisons outside Parkinson disease. The dyspepsia trial reports a week-four epigastric pain score of 0.38 with anise versus 2.05 with cornstarch. The COVID-19 study's modeled ratio remains ambiguous. Methanolic extract assays add preclinical context. The minimal lean against worsening concerns gastrointestinal pain with uncertain transfer.

Post-COVID and post-traumatic studies use thyme in multi-odor programs. They report whole-program olfactory comparisons. Thyme oil in an EEG biometric conference study serves as one of several identification odors. The direction for consuming fresh thyme and Parkinson olfaction remains open.

The small Himalayan raspberry series reports lower pressure with medication changes and no orthostatic symptom measurement. The vinegar abstract describes scheduled pressure tests without results. A black raspberry slurry trial reports adverse events by crossover sequence and supplies no posture-specific estimate. The frozen raspberry lightheadedness direction remains open.

The dried-thyme trial reports more students with normal-range HADS anxiety at one month than starch. Its stated SD is incompatible with baseline severity counts, and the printed category cutoffs overlap and the registry reports a different enrollment and masking design. The descriptive lean remains minimal, with an inconclusive wild-thyme extract comparison and no Parkinson-specific estimate.

Parkinson diet reports pool berries or give intake separately from voice. The boysenberry–apple intervention's speech complaint was in a composite outcome. An external hoarseness use appears in a blackberry flower-bud assay report without measured voice. Frozen blackberry and Parkinson voice loudness remain unresolved.

Isolated thymoquinone and Nigella extract studies report findings across animal movement and imposed-posture tasks. The additional extract study gives a catalepsy contrast without measured movement speed. These different models and preparations leave ground Nigella and clinical Parkinson bradykinesia unresolved.

The dried-thyme trial measures self-rated memory. Isolated thymol experiments report animal behavioral comparisons, and thyme oil studies report experimental cholinergic signaling. The direction of fresh thyme and clinical attention in Parkinson disease remains open.
